# Brad Jacobs (businessman) Brad Jacobs (businessman) American businessman (born 1956) | Brad Jacobs | | --- | | [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/5/54/Brad_Jacobs_XPO%2C_GXO%2C_RXO_chairman.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brad_Jacobs_XPO,_GXO,_RXO_chairman.jpg) | | Born | (1956-08-03) August 3, 1956 (age69)
[Providence, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), U.S. | | Education | [Northfield Mount Hermon School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northfield_Mount_Hermon_School "Northfield Mount Hermon School") | | Almamater | [Bennington College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bennington_College "Bennington College")
[Brown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_University "Brown University") | | Occupation | Businessman | **Brad Jacobs** (born August 3, 1956) is an American businessman and entrepreneur[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-1) who is chairman and CEO of QXO, Inc.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Time-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:2-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-7) He has founded eight separate billion-dollar companies, including [XPO Logistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPO_Logistics "XPO Logistics"), [United Rentals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Rentals "United Rentals"), and United Waste. He is the author of the book, _How to Make a Few Billion Dollars_, published in 2024.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-8) A sequel, _How to Make a Few_ More _Billion Dollars,_ came out in 2025.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-11) Jacobs is a member of [Business Roundtable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_Roundtable "Business Roundtable"), [The Business Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Business_Council "The Business Council"), and [The Economic Club of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Economic_Club_of_New_York "The Economic Club of New York"). ## Early life and education Jacobs was born in [Providence, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"), to Charlotte Sybil (née Bander) and Albert Jordan Jacobs.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Charlotte-12)[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Albert-13) Jacobs' father was a fashion jewelry importer.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Albert-13) After graduating from [Northfield Mount Hermon School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northfield_Mount_Hermon_School "Northfield Mount Hermon School") in [Gill, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill,_Massachusetts "Gill, Massachusetts"), he attended [Bennington College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bennington_College "Bennington College") in [Bennington, Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bennington,_Vermont "Bennington, Vermont") and [Brown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_University "Brown University") in [Providence, Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Providence,_Rhode_Island "Providence, Rhode Island"). He studied math and music, but he dropped out in 1976.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-14) ## Career ### Amerex Oil Associates (1979–1983) In 1979,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:3-15) Jacobs co-founded Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage firm.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-stamfordadvocate2005-16) He was the company's CEO until it was sold in 1983. In 1984, he moved to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and founded Hamilton Resources, where he conducted oil trading deals.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-SA_Greenwich-17) Jacobs has frequently recognized [Ludwig Jesselson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Jesselson "Ludwig Jesselson") as being an influential mentor.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Antoine-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-19) ### United Waste Systems (1989–1997) In 1989, Jacobs founded United Waste Systems in [Greenwich, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich,_Connecticut "Greenwich, Connecticut") and began consolidating small waste collection companies that had overlapping routes in rural areas. He was chairman and CEO; in 1992 he took the company public.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-fundinguniverse1-20) He sold United Waste Systems to USA Waste Services for $2.5 billion in August 1997.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:3-15) ### United Rentals (1997) In September 1997, Jacobs formed United Rentals becoming the chairman and chief executive officer of the company. During late 1997 and early 1998, the company grew through a strategy of consolidating equipment rental dealers in North America.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-21) He took the company public in December 1997 on the [New York Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Stock_Exchange "New York Stock Exchange").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Antoine-18) ### XPO In 2011, he invested approximately $150 million in XPO (then named _Express-1 Expedited Solutions_), a transportation and [third-party logistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-party_logistics "Third-party logistics") provider.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-reuters-22) He became chairman of the board and CEO and gained ownership of approximately 71 percent of the company. The company was later listed on the NYSE under the ticker symbol XPO.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-23) Jacobs subsequently led the $7 billion spin-off of GXO Logistics in 2021, and the $5 billion spin-off of RXO in 2022.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-24) ### QXO (2024–present) In June 2024, Jacobs founded QXO with the intention to consolidate the $800 billion building products distribution industry.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:2-6)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-25) With the launch, he raised over $5 billion in equity. That included what [_Bloomberg_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News") said was the largest equity offering ever in the building products sector and the largest ever [private investment in public equity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_investment_in_public_equity "Private investment in public equity") (PIPE) for an industrial company.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:0-26)[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-27) In April 2025, QXO acquired [Beacon Building Products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beacon_Building_Products "Beacon Building Products"), the second-largest distributor of roofing, waterproofing, and related exterior building products in North America, for approximately $11 billion.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:4-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:5-29) In April 2026, QXO acquired Kodiak Building Partners,[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:4-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:5-29)the fourth-largest distributor of lumber and complementary building materials in the United States, for $2.25 billion.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:4-28)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-:5-29)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-31) In July 2026, QXO acquired TopBuild, the largest distributor and installer of insulation and specialty building products in North America, for approximately $17 billion.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-32) ## Personal life Brad Jacobs and his wife live in [Greenwich, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenwich,_Connecticut "Greenwich, Connecticut")[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Antoine-18) and they have four children. He is an art collector and owns art by [Picasso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Picasso "Pablo Picasso"), [de Kooning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willem_de_Kooning "Willem de Kooning"), [Calder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Calder "Alexander Calder"), [Lichtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Lichtenstein "Roy Lichtenstein"), and other artists.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-Antoine-18) ## Bibliography - _How to Make a Few Billion Dollars;_ Austin: Greenleaf Book Group Press, 2024; [ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN_(identifier) "ISBN (identifier)") [979-8886451740](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/979-8886451740 "Special:BookSources/979-8886451740")[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Jacobs_(businessman)#cite_note-33) - _How to Make a Few_ More _Billion Dollars_; Austin: Greenleaf Book Group Press, 2025; [ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN_(identifier) "ISBN (identifier)") [979-8-88645-465-9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/979-8-88645-465-9 "Special:BookSources/979-8-88645-465-9") ## References 01. metadata.description: Brad Jacobs is an American businessman and entrepreneur who is chairman and CEO of QXO, Inc. He has founded eight separate billion-dollar companies, including XPO Logistics, United Rentals, and United Waste. He is the author of the book, How to Make a Few Billion Dollars, published in 2024. A sequel, How to Make a Few More Billion Dollars, came out in 2025. Jacobs is a member of Business Roundtable, The Business Council, and The Economic Club of New York.
